### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/rest`, touching **10** documentable anchor(s).

**23** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bee75cebe63889f93fa1e6dc358cd8c5f7b9a928`.

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `/data/:object (route, 64 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **15** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bee75cebe63889f93fa1e6dc358cd8c5f7b9a928` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7ba63ebbcd79daf71ffbf91e44fb7c18209e941d` — the merge of head `132e93c05bd736c80a166cff38955b910ec8cdf9` into base `bee75cebe63889f93fa1e6dc358cd8c5f7b9a928`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7ba63ebbcd79daf71ffbf91e44fb7c18209e941d && git checkout 7ba63ebbcd79daf71ffbf91e44fb7c18209e941d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin bee75cebe63889f93fa1e6dc358cd8c5f7b9a928 132e93c05bd736c80a166cff38955b910ec8cdf9 && git checkout -B drift-repro bee75cebe63889f93fa1e6dc358cd8c5f7b9a928 && git merge --no-ff 132e93c05bd736c80a166cff38955b910ec8cdf9

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bee75cebe63889f93fa1e6dc358cd8c5f7b9a928
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs bee75cebe63889f93fa1e6dc358cd8c5f7b9a928` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `132e93c05bd736c80a166cff38955b910ec8cdf9`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #20701 body and all sixteen comments (governing: `5897601448`, `5906762084`, `5910777625`, `5917724406`, `5918402332`, `5919618026`; context: PR #20905 landed as `165c1d49e3` and its record `5916269679`); PR #20941 body, file list (3 files: `packages/rest/src/import-runner.ts` +38/-4, `packages/rest/src/import-row-schema-drift-20701.test.ts` new, `.changeset/20701-import-row-schema-drift-door-answer.md` new) and the net diff `67c1b11a20...132e93c05b` (260 insertions, 4 deletions, two commits); the check-runs on the head, polled to convergence. Source premises were read on the merge-base `67c1b11a20` by `git show`; nothing was built, run, checked out or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

**(a) `toFailedResult` asks the create door's own mapper, and adopts only its `INVALID_FIELD` verdict — right, and it is the same mapper, not a second rule.**
- Same mapper, same argument. The create door is the `POST ${dataPath}/:object` handler (`rest-server.ts:8764-8765` on the merge-base) and its catch answers `mapDataError(error, req.params?.object)` (`:8806`); the row now calls `mapDataError(err, objectName)` with the object being imported. The import derives nothing about the field or the column itself: which arm fires, what `field` is, and the sentence are all the mapper's. The `door.code === 'INVALID_FIELD'` test is an adoption gate on the verdict, not a classification, so triage's ⛔ "no second rule inside the import" (`5897601448`) holds. `mapDataError` is `withDeclaredUserMessage(error, classifyDataError(error, object))` (`error-response.ts:680-682`) and neither function logs or writes anything (no `logger`/`console` call in `:1276-1990`), so calling it per failed row is side-effect free; `./error-response.js` was already imported for `isEngineDuplicateRecordEnvelope`, so no new import edge.
- Partial adoption is right for this claim. The claim (`5918402332`) pins "a unique conflict and a not-null row keep today's answers (controls)", and the dev measured that full adoption moves both: the 409 arm (`error-response.ts:1110`) REPLACES the engine's sentence with the curated one and ships the engine's as `developerMessage`, and the NOT NULL branch (`:1809-1832`) answers `VALIDATION_FAILED` with a `required` finding and a `hint` where the row relays the driver's code. Taking every verdict would have breached the claim's controls; the consequence, two sentence sources inside one row report, is escalated under ③ items 2 and 3.
- No error that answered a different row today becomes `INVALID_FIELD` wrongly. The mapper has exactly three ways to say `INVALID_FIELD`: the structured arm for an envelope with `code === 'INVALID_FIELD'` that is not sandbox-origin (`:1261-1273`), the driver-string missing-column branch (`:1787-1807`), and the sandbox unwrap relaying a declared code through `thrownCodeFields` (`:495-500`). Each, read against the merge-base:
  - An undeclared key: the engine's declared-field door throws `code: 'INVALID_FIELD'`, `field`, `fields` as bare strings, message `Unknown field 'k' on object 'X'` (`engine.ts:1860-1868`). `fields[0]` is a string, so `first` is `undefined` and the door is asked; the structured arm relays `String(error.message)`, the same `code` and the same `field`. Before, the row read `e.code`, `e.field` and `sanitizeRowError(message)`, which is `message.slice(0, 300)` for this text (`looksLikeSql` matches only a statement-leading message, `import-runner.ts:237-239`). Byte-identical unless the key name is itself around 270 characters; then the row now carries the door's untruncated sentence, which is the door's answer. Pinned as a control on `code` and `field` by `import-row-report-field-20701.test.ts` (in the dev's ablation, those pins stayed green). Right; the dry run reaches the same arm through `previewVerdict`'s throw and reads the same.
  - A validation finding: `ValidationError.fields[]` holds objects, `first` is defined, the door is never asked; unchanged. An empty `fields[]` asks the door, which answers `VALIDATION_FAILED`, not adopted, so the old rule runs. Right.
  - An error already carrying `field`: the engine's `DuplicateRecordError` answers the 409 `UNIQUE_VIOLATION` arm, not adopted, so the row keeps `UNIQUE_VIOLATION`, `field` and the engine's sentence (pinned control). A read door's `INVALID_FIELD` from the upsert match lookup (`findExisting`, same object, `import-runner.ts:528-546`) takes the structured arm and reads as before on `code` and `field`. The reference resolver swallows every `findData` throw (`resolveRef`'s lookup `catch`, `:502`), so a REFERENCED object's drifted column never reaches `toFailedResult`, and the sentence's object name is always the imported object's. Right.
  - Non-SQLite driver text: MySQL `Unknown column 'c'` (unanchored) and Postgres `column "c" of relation "t" does not exist` (`matchMissingColumnOfRelation`, `packages/types/src/relation-sub-object.ts:91`) classify into the same missing-column arm with `field` from the capture; that is the same class and the same answer the door gives on those dialects. NOT NULL text in all three dialects goes to `VALIDATION_FAILED`, a missing relation to `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` or the 500 fault, none adopted. Right; unmeasured on Postgres and MySQL, as the PR body says.
  - A sandboxed producer declaring `INVALID_FIELD` with no finding: `SandboxError` carries `innerMessage`, `code`, `fields`, `status`, `userMessage` and no `field` (`quickjs-runner.ts:1591-1640`). Before, the row relayed the QuickJS debug wrapper through `sanitizeRowError(e.message)`; now the sandbox unwrap's body (`error: innerMessage`, `code: 'INVALID_FIELD'`) is adopted, so the row carries the business sentence, still with no `field`. That is the door's answer and the direction the card wants; unmeasured by the dev, and not in the changeset. Residue, not a verdict mover.

**(b) Both call sites pass the right object, and the dry run is untouched.** `objectName` is the runner's own option (`import-runner.ts:424`). The flush call (`:813`) covers every bulk-insert outcome (`insertManyData` per-row outcomes, `createManyData` degradation, `writeOne`); the per-row catch (`:929`) covers the upsert's update path (`updateData`, `:895`), the non-bulk `createData` (`:919`), `findExisting`, `coerceRow` and `previewVerdict`. The sync route and the job worker both run `runImport`, so the async job's rows come through the same two sites, and the results route is pinned. On the dry run `previewVerdict` asks `validateData`, which reads metadata and never the table, so a drifted column raises no driver error there and its preview row (`ok`/`created`) is unchanged, as the PR states and the pin file's docblock refuses to vouch for; an undeclared key on the dry run reads as before per (a). Right.

**(c) Row shape: existing keys only, and the sentence is safe.** The adopted literal is `row`, `ok`, `action`, `error`, `code` plus a conditional `field`, every one an existing key of `ImportRowResultSchema` (`packages/spec/src/api/export.zod.ts:322-331`); the door's `object`, `hint`, `userMessage` and `developerMessage` are not copied, so no key is added. `String(door.error)` is safe: both `INVALID_FIELD` arms always set a string `error`. The sentence is fixed text plus a `[a-z0-9_]+` capture and the object name, never the driver's raw text; the object name equals the table name (Prime Directive 6) and the old row already relayed `table proj_probe has no column named late` verbatim (measured by the dev; `looksLikeSql` does not match it), so nothing is exposed that the old row did not already expose. `os migrate` is a real command. Right.

**(d) Changeset (`@objectstack/rest` patch): accurate, and it claims nothing undelivered.** Every claim is pinned or verified above: the sync route and the async job's rows; `INVALID_FIELD`, `field` and the door's sentence; the old driver code and text; "the same mapper as the create door", adopted for `INVALID_FIELD` only; unique-conflict and NOT NULL rows unchanged; the dry run still previews the row as `ok`. Two omissions, neither a false claim: the sandbox-producer case in (a), and the undeclared-key sentence no longer being cut at 300 characters. The `(#20701)` in the title follows the existing changeset convention.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: no` with `patch` is right. `code`, `field` and `error` are existing optional keys of `ImportRowResultSchema`, filled with different values on one class of failed rows; no key is added, no row that failed now succeeds or the reverse, and `INVALID_FIELD` is a value the row already emits for an undeclared key, so no vocabulary widens. A driver-dialect code such as `SQLITE_ERROR` was never contract vocabulary (ADR-0112). AGENTS.md: a bug fix in a released package takes `patch`. The claim's own Clause-② reading (`5918402332`) says the same and the dev re-read it against the real diff.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev `deviations`, each answered:
1. vitest dropped `--maxWorkers=2` after a bare `--`; the whole local project still ran. The documented trap, no reading lost; `Test Core` on the head is the gate. Accepted.
2. `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` NOT MEASURED locally (needs every package's `dist/`). `Lint & Repo Gates` and `Build Core` on the head cover it. Accepted.
3. The NOT NULL control pin asserts the driver's own code `SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_NOTNULL` as "unchanged by this PR", not as right, and the docblock says a converging card flips it. An honest characterisation pin of the control the claim named; it will be rewritten by whichever card takes ③ item 2. Accepted.
4. Commit trailers are the model-free pair (`Claude-Session` plus `Co-authored-by: Claude`) on both commits `4f650c6ecd` and `132e93c05b`, as AGENTS.md requires over the harness reminder; no model identifier in the title, body, changeset or code. Accepted.

Dev `out_of_scope_findings`, each answered or escalated:
1. **Dry-run preview of a drifted column answers `ok`/`created` while the commit fails it (class a, measured on both bases) — ESCALATED to the dispatching seat, for triage.** It is the card's title family (the Path line, "an import preview promises only rows the commit will write") but not inside the confirmed REST scope: `5906762084` fixed the REST half at three items, `5917724406` folded item 4 as the commit and async rows only, and the maintainer's 「20701 同意」 confirmed that scope. The fix cannot be REST's: the preview's verdict is `engine.validate`'s, which reads metadata and never the physical column set, and the create door has no preview at all, so a REST-side table read would be exactly the second rule triage forbade (⛔ `5897601448`, ⛔ `5906762084`). The layer is the engine lane (`ObjectQL.validate`, or the write path's own pre-driver check) consulting the driver's known column set, the way #20805 was cut as a `domain:engine` child; whether the platform wants the preview to detect drift at all, or leaves drift to `os migrate`, is triage's or the maintainer's call. The dev's class and reach are right. Not a verdict mover.
2. **A NOT NULL row relays the driver's code where the door answers `VALIDATION_FAILED` with a `required` finding (class a, measured) — ESCALATED, as a candidate REST item.** Inside the card's goal as triage framed item 4 ("the import row answers what the create door answers"), in the same function, and one adoption-gate widening away: the door's `fields[0]` is `{ field, code: 'required' }`, which the row's finding-wins rule already renders. But triage's item-4 sentence defines the item by the drift case and the claim named NOT NULL a control, so it was outside this claim and the dev was right to leave it. It also puts a driver-dialect code (`SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_NOTNULL`; `23502` and `ER_BAD_NULL_ERROR` on the other dialects) on the wire `code`, an ADR-0112 vocabulary concern in its own right. Triage decides whether it becomes REST item 5 and the control pin flips with it. Not a verdict mover.
3. **Unique-conflict sentence, wording only.** Same `code` and `field` at both doors; the row carries the engine's sentence, the door the curated one with the engine's as `developerMessage`. The unnamed case already deliberately shares the door's wording (`UNNAMED_CONFLICT`, `import-runner.ts:254`). "Noted, not filed" is right under Prime Directive 10 (no defect, no contract violation); it rides with item 2 if triage takes that. Not a verdict mover.
4. **Postgres read-path template unmatched (source reading, not measured).** Confirmed on the merge-base: `matchMissingColumnOfRelation` is anchored to `column "c" of relation "t" does not exist` and its docblock says the read-path `column "c" does not exist` "does not match, and it does not need to" (`relation-sub-object.ts:68-93`). The reach is the upsert match lookup on a drifted `matchFields` column under Postgres, a read the door itself answers the same way, so it is the mapper's pre-existing gap, not this PR's. Without a repro it has no card evidence; the live-Postgres lane exists if the seat wants one. "Noted" is right. Not a verdict mover.

File list: three paths, none a governed surface (`Governed Surface Queue Guard` success); head repo is the base repo; the PR is a draft, per the dispatch; first line `Part of #20701` with no closing keyword (`Part-of PR must not also close its card` success); `Check Changeset` success.

Check-runs on `132e93c05b` (converged 2026-09-30T21:13:58Z; 34 runs, collapsed to latest-per-name): 31 `success`, 3 `skipped` (`Build Docs`, `Console Pin Gate`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`), 0 failure, 0 in progress. The seven required contexts are all `success`: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check` (rollup, with `Type Check · consumer gates`, `debt ledger`, `source gates`, `workspace`), `Test Core` (rollup and shards 1-6), `Dogfood Regression Gate` (rollup and 1-3), `Build Core`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`.
